So good evening. I'm excited to share with you the annual data update for the substitute program during the 22-23 school year and provide some insight on what's next for this program. So the data found on this slide highlights substitute stats from the 22-23 school year.

As of June 8th, LCPS had 3,274 active substitutes available to work. This represents a 7% increase over last year. During the 22-23 school year, 2,564 substitutes worked at least one job assignment during the school year, which is greater than 400 substitutes working at least one job assignment last school year.

During the 2022-23 school year, 1,295 long-term substitute positions were filled with substitutes. Two of the most significant in numbers you will find on this slide include the hiring of 1,216 additional substitutes this year, nearly doubling the number of substitutes hired from last year.

As we continue to leverage technology and increase efficiencies within the hiring process and onboarding, we hope to only see additional increases. And the fact that 289 of our active substitutes have been hired into licensed teaching positions, a number that more than doubled from last year and indicates the value in this candidate pool as a viable pipeline for filling positions within the county. The data found on this chart

provides a snapshot of substitute fill rates on an average school day during the 2022-23 school year. As you can see, the adjusted fill rate found in the very last column differs quite significantly from the fill rate column next to it. This difference is based on the adjustment made for the site-assigned substitutes located at schools. The site-assigned substitutes are used to fill the unfilled teacher-requested subjobs at the school. Both the fill rate and adjusted fill rate increased

by four percentage points when compared to last school year. On average, the number of unfilled jobs for teachers identified as 189 in total is less than two per school. Although substitutes largely support teachers. Substitutes are also currently available for teacher assistants, library assistants, nurses, nurse assistants, health clinic specialists, school-based clerical positions, and administrators. assigned substitutes, we are able to adjust our fill rate and provide for a greater number of teachers needing coverage. For background, site-assigned substitutes were created during the 2020-21 school year to assist during the return to in-person learning after the pandemic.

In general, site-assigned substitutes are provided to schools on a 25 to 1 teacher-to-substitute ratio. However, based on the level of need or the inability for a school to regularly obtain subs to provide coverage for teachers, HRTD will work with those schools to provide additional site assigned substitutes. For the 22-23 school year, all site assigned substitute jobs available were filled. To create greater consistency among schools and care for our subs, as well as our

site assigned subs, HRTD, DOI, and the Department of School Leadership is currently working to collaborate to create greater guidance for schools on the sub usage within their buildings. As you may recall, it was just a short time ago that the Substitute Incentive Program was created.

We are delighted to report that more subs are picking up jobs since the implementation of these incentives just a short time ago on November 1st, 2021. The 22-23 school year is the first full school year with both incentives available. High volume days are defined as those school days that have historically had higher than normal requests for substitutes. Examples would be a Friday before a three-day weekend or a single workday between a weekend and a mid-week holiday.

During the 22-23 school year, 26 days were identified as high volume days. As far as the loyalty rate is concerned. A substitute qualifies for the loyalty program once they have worked a minimum of 25 job assignments. They do not have to be consecutive. On their 26th assignment and every assignment after that during that school year, they would then be eligible for the increased

rate. So what's next for the substitute program? So much more than I have time to share tonight on one slide, so please expect more to come in the beginning of the next school year.
